name: Inverse Marcus-Gunn Phenomenon

criteria.description: Synkinetic elevation of the upper eyelid on jaw opening or lateral jaw movements
Absence of classical Marcus-Gunn jaw-winking phenomenon (eyelid elevation on jaw closure)
Congenital presentation with no history of trauma or surgery
Electromyographic evidence of aberrant trigeminal-oculomotor innervation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of synkinetic eyelid elevation on jaw opening with absence of classical Marcus-Gunn jaw-winking, preferably congenital onset
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electromyography can aid in confirming aberrant innervation but is not mandatory.

imaging: MRI may show aberrant innervation pathways in cranial nerves
Electromyography demonstrating synkinetic activity between trigeminal and oculomotor nerves
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations; presumed sporadic congenital aberrant innervation
other: Clinical observation of eyelid movement in relation to jaw activity is diagnostic

distinguishingFeatures: Eyelid elevation on jaw closure instead of jaw opening
Absence of synkinetic eyelid movement with jaw motion
No synkinetic eyelid movement related to jaw activity

redFlags: Sudden onset of eyelid synkinesis in adulthood
Progressive worsening of eyelid or facial movement
Associated neurological deficits such as facial numbness or weakness
